About this document

This document provides the teaching content for Further Mathematics Year 13 of the
New Zealand Curriculum. Equivalent for Te Marautanga o Aotearoa is being
published separately.

Progress and assessment information for Further Mathematics Year 13 is still in
development. Once that is completed, Further Mathematics Year 13 is proposed to be
made by the Minister of Education as a National Curriculum Statement under section
90(1)(a) of the Education and Training Act 2020.

It is proposed that, once made and published in the New Zealand Gazette, schools
who offer Further Mathematics Year 13 will be required to start using it in Year 13
from 1 January 2030.

This document will be replaced with the official version made under the Act and
published in the New Zealand Gazette once that has occurred.

Purpose statement                                                             Ānō me he whare pūngāwerewere.   Behold, it is like the web of a spider.




  In Further Mathematics, students are taught mathematical ideas that underpin
  concepts such as number theory, graph theory, and logic. Students are taught the
  processes behind mathematical thinking and abstract reasoning, enabling them
  to engage in authentic structured problem-solving.


Through the study of Further Mathematics, students are taught to use logical
reasoning, problem-solving, and mathematical skills to support them to make
informed and deliberate connections between theory and practice. They apply
concepts, techniques, and calculations to interpret and simplify mathematical
problems.
Further Mathematics provides students with the knowledge and practices to construct
and communicate mathematical arguments, investigate patterns, relationships, and
properties of numbers. They apply rigorous mathematical reasoning to theoretical and
contextual problems. This disciplinary knowledge enables students to represent,
visualise, and analyse sets and graphs, and to model, solve, and verify differential
equations.
As students progress through Further Mathematics Year 13, they are taught to
develop increasingly sophisticated skills in logic, proof construction, abstraction,
mathematical modelling, and problem-solving, while building a deeper understanding
of number systems, discrete structures and systems described by differential
equations. This bridges theoretical mathematical theory and practical application
enabling students to critically evaluate, verify, and refine mathematical solutions.

  Further Mathematics leads to pathways in mathematics and related areas, such
  as computer science, software engineering, advanced mathematics, physics,
  complex systems, algorithm design, and engineering.
